_comment: Training presets, sized against measured throughput on the RTX 3060 in this
machine. `config` is a TrainConfig body: POST it to the LLM engine's /train, or
save it through the backend's /training/presets to get it into the UI.
`dimensions` and `ctx_window` must be powers of two — the backend rejects
anything else (jobs.rs) and the frontend edits them as exponents. `layers` is
free, which makes depth the knob for hitting a time budget.
Sizing rule: Chinchilla puts the compute-optimal point at ~20 training tokens
per parameter. Parameters means non-embedding — with a tied 8k-vocab table the
embedding is a lookup, not compute, and counting it would size the corpus for
arithmetic that never happens. Each preset trains exactly one epoch, so no
See README, 'Sizing a run', for which figures are measured and which are not.

presets.name: Chinchilla 1
presets.notes: The compute-optimal run that fits in an hour. 16.80M params, 12.60M non-embedding; 252M tokens at 20.0 per non-embedding parameter, one epoch, 30.8k steps, ~0.87h. Step cost is interpolated (see README), so treat the hour as +/-10%. Repacks first: the corpus on disk is 391M tokens and this wants 252M, so the FineWeb cap of 3531 files trims it — budget 10-20 min before the first step.

presets.name: Chinchilla 1 (whole corpus)
presets.notes: The same rule applied to the corpus already on disk, so nothing is repacked and the step cost is measured rather than interpolated. 23.10M params, 18.90M non-embedding; all 391M tokens at 20.7 per non-embedding parameter, 47.7k steps, ~1.66h, 1.6 GiB VRAM.

presets.name: Smoke
presets.notes: Deliberately not compute-optimal — a few minutes of training to prove the pipeline end to end, not a model worth keeping. 5.25M params, 3.15M non-embedding, 38M tokens (12x its trunk, well past Chinchilla). Repacks 500 FineWeb files first, which is quick.
